checks.category: GXCat G X bundles a carrier : Type with topology, ChartedSpace X and HasGroupoid as instance fields. `GXCat.category` sets Hom V W := {f : V → W // IsGXMorphism G X f}, with id, comp, id_comp, comp_id and assoc all by rfl. In scratch, `(V ⟶ W) = {f : V → W // IsGXMorphism (GSR n) (S n) f}` holds by rfl for LocProj n. It is a genuine category. Its morphisms are exactly the maps that are continuous and, in charts near every point, the restriction of an element of G: the (G,X)-local isomorphisms. GXCat.isLocalHomeomorph_hom proves each is a local homeomorphism, and isGXMorphism_iff_jets proves the class equals the paper's « J(V₂)∘f ⊂ J(V₁) » for continuous f. Both objects share one model X, so they have the same dimension, as in plan F5
checks.morphism_jets: isGXMorphism_iff_jets is correctly stated: the composite germ is γ.compTendsto f, over all γ ∈ J(V₂) at f x. The continuity hypothesis is forced, because composing germs needs f to tend to f x. The reading is disclosed
checks.pullback: existsUnique_pullback: for p : M → N an IsLocalHomeomorph (« ouvert étalé », kb/0001), it gives ∃ structure on M with HasGroupoid and p a morphism, and every structure with p a morphism has the same maximal atlas. That is « l'unique structure telle que la projection soit un morphisme ». Correct; the covering case is a corollary (IsCoveringMap.isLocalHomeomorph)
checks.pushforward: existsUnique_pushforward: for p surjective, a local homeomorphism, and IsGXDeck, it gives existence plus uniqueness up to maximal atlas. IsGXDeck says every local deck transformation x ↦ x′ over p is a (G,X)-map near x. That is the right hypothesis: without it, the transitions of the pushed charts are not in G. Correct

It assumes ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul Γ V, ContinuousConstSMul Γ V, IsCancelSMul Γ V (free = « sans point fixe »), T2Space V and LocallyCompactSpace V, plus each γ • · an IsGXMorphism (« groupe … d'automorphismes »). isGXMorphism_quotientMk and maximalAtlas_quotient_unique give « l'unique structure pour laquelle la projection … soit un morphisme ». checks.proper_discontinuity: Mathlib's ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul says that for compact K, L, {γ | γK ∩ L ≠ ∅} is finite. On a locally compact Hausdorff V this is the compact-set formulation the French school used around 1960 (Cartan; Bourbaki's « proprement » for a discrete group). The auditor's knowledge here is not checked against a source in the hub. The weaker 'wandering' sense — every point has U with γU ∩ U = ∅ for γ ≠ 1 — is Mathlib's IsQuotientCoveringMap.disjoint (Topology/Covering/Quotient.lean:38-41), and it already suffices for a (G,X)-structure on V/Γ, although V/Γ may then fail to be Hausdorff. Verified in scratch: from `hq : IsQuotientCoveringMap (Quotient.mk (orbitRel Γ V)) Γ` and hΓ, `existsUnique_pushforward hq.isCoveringMap.isLocalHomeomorph Quotient.mk_surjective (isGXDeck_quotientMk hΓ)` elaborates, with no T2 or local compactness (issue 1)

issues.problem: The author's question on « proprement discontinu » has a code-independent answer that the file does not record. The structure on V/Γ exists, uniquely, already under the weakest sense: the wandering neighbourhood condition, i.e. Mathlib's IsQuotientCoveringMap. Mathlib's ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul with T2 and local compactness is needed only to make V/Γ Hausdorff, i.e. a « variété » in plan F6's sense
issues.fix: Add `theorem existsUnique_quotient_of_isQuotientCoveringMap (hq : IsQuotientCoveringMap (Quotient.mk (MulAction.orbitRel Γ V)) Γ) (hΓ …) := existsUnique_pushforward hq.isCoveringMap.isLocalHomeomorph Quotient.mk_surjective (isGXDeck_quotientMk hΓ)` (verified). Narrow the question to: 'is V/G required to be Hausdorff (then Mathlib's sense), or only a (G,X)-space (then the weaker sense, proved too)?'

issues.problem: The objects carry no connectedness, Hausdorffness or second countability. The paper's objects are « variétés » (plan F6: connected, T2, second countable). That is fine for this groundwork, but § 2's « isomorphisme fonctoriel » (DEC-113: a CategoryTheory.Equivalence) is between categories of variétés. An equivalence built on GXCat would prove a different, more general statement, and the cone side's analogue may fail for non-T2 objects (Hausdorffness of B = V/ℝ₊*, plan § 2)
issues.fix: Record in SCOPE that the § 2 equivalence will use the full subcategory of GXCat on connected T2 (second countable) objects, e.g. `CategoryTheory.FullSubcategory (fun V : GXCat G X => ConnectedSpace V ∧ T2Space V)`. Decide this before wave 4

fidelity_summary: The prose of p. 238 is formalized faithfully where it is formalized. Morphisms (by charts, equivalent to the jet definition for continuous maps) form a genuine category of local (G,X)-isomorphisms. The quotient by a properly discontinuous free group of automorphisms carries a unique structure making the projection a morphism. Every « ouvert étalé » (local homeomorphism) and every covering carries the unique pulled-back structure. Not formalized, and disclosed: « si R est galoisien, V est le quotient … » and the universal covering's projection (Prop. 2, wave 3). No label, nothing marked.
questions_for_author: « proprement discontinu »: must V/G be Hausdorff (Mathlib's ProperlyDiscontinuousSMul with T2 and locally compact V, the compact-set sense of the period), or is the weaker wandering sense intended? With issue 1's one-liner, the structure is proved in both cases and only Hausdorffness of V/G depends on the choice.
For § 2's equivalence (DEC-113): restrict to connected Hausdorff (second countable) objects, i.e. a full subcategory of GXCat, as plan F6 reads « variété »?
